t: You are standing at the tomb of Marthe and Sir William Goscombe John, in Hampstead Cemetery. Sir William is buried here, and he made the tomb himself. He was a Welsh sculptor, best known for public memorials. He first won national attention with statues of eminent Victorians in London and Cardiff. After the Boer War and the First World War he created a large number of war memorials. Two of them, The Response 1914 in Newcastle and the Port Sunlight War Memorial, are considered the finest sculptural groups on any British monument.
